title: Subeg Singh gains authority and the Nawab soon dies

blocks.text: When the Nawab asked him what reward he desired, Subeg Singh declined mere personal favour and instead asked for a state coin to be struck in his name along with effective political authority. He wanted gains that could actually protect the Panth rather than flatter one man.

Armed with that leverage, Subeg Singh Jambar moved quickly against the machinery of persecution. The gallows dismantled, punishments were reversed, and the public signs of state terror against Sikhs began to disappear from Lahore.

The Nawab died without further torment soon afterward, exactly as Bhai Taru Singh’s word had implied. Hindus and Singhs read that death as proof that the Guru had upheld Sikhi's honour, while many Muslims took it as a sign that their old confidence in power had been shaken.
